name: Chest pain / collapse
summary: A crewmate has chest pain, or has collapsed.

pre.title: Call it out
pre.detail: Announce “medical emergency” on the crew loop. The Crew Medical Officer leads.

pre.title: Secure patient and rescuer
pre.detail: In weightlessness you will both drift. Use the medical restraint, foot loops or a wall.

pre.title: Check response and breathing (10 s max)
pre.detail: Tap the shoulders, call their name, and look for normal breathing.

steps.title: Start CPR now
steps.detail: Use the restraint for back support, or the Evetts–Russomano handstand: feet braced on the wall, hands on the chest, push with your legs.

steps.title: Attach the defibrillator (AED)
steps.detail: Follow its voice prompts. Everyone stays clear while it analyses and shocks.

steps.title: Keep the cycles going
steps.detail: Swap compressors every 2 minutes. ASTRA timestamps each step for the ground team.

steps.title: Rest and monitor
steps.detail: Keep them still and calm. Attach the monitor. HR, BP and SpO2 are logged every 5 minutes.

steps.title: Onboard cardiac checklist
steps.detail: Give oxygen or medications only as written in the flight-surgeon-approved protocol.

steps.title: Record what happened
steps.detail: Note when it started, what the pain feels like, where it spreads, and any other symptoms.

steps.title: Be ready to switch to CPR
steps.detail: If they stop responding or stop breathing normally, switch to the other track.

post.title: Priority packet to ground
post.detail: Initial priority alert sent automatically at T+0. Step timeline is transmitted upon completion.

post.title: Act now, update later
post.detail: Don't wait for Earth. Follow the protocol and send updates as things change.

note: Microgravity CPR: the Evetts–Russomano method was co-developed by Brazilian researcher Thais Russomano.

name: Breathing difficulty
summary: A crewmate is short of breath, or an atmosphere alarm is sounding.

pre.title: Call it out
pre.detail: Announce the emergency. One crew member checks the cabin atmosphere displays.

pre.title: Check the air first
pre.detail: Is there a CO2, ammonia, smoke or pressure alarm? Protect yourself before helping.

steps.title: Masks on
steps.detail: Put on emergency masks or oxygen for everyone, patient first if they can't.

steps.title: Move to a safe module
steps.detail: Follow the alarm checklist and close the hatch behind you.

steps.title: Monitor SpO2 and breathing
steps.detail: Measure every 5 minutes. ASTRA logs the values.

steps.title: Upright and anchored
steps.detail: Restrain them in an upright position and keep them calm.

steps.title: Measure SpO2 and breathing rate
steps.detail: Repeat every 5 minutes. Below 90% means the oxygen protocol.

steps.title: Look for a cause
steps.detail: Allergy, asthma, chest injury or infection: follow the matching onboard checklist.

post.title: Priority packet to ground
post.detail: Initial priority alert sent automatically at T+0. Step timeline is transmitted upon completion.

post.title: Act now, update later
post.detail: Don't wait for Earth. Keep monitoring and send updates.

note: Dust from the Moon and Mars is fine and sharp, so always rule it out after an EVA.

name: Head injury / unconscious
summary: A crewmate hit their head or was found unresponsive.

pre.title: Call it out
pre.detail: Announce the emergency. The CMO leads.

pre.title: Protect the neck
pre.detail: Avoid twisting the head and neck. Use the collar from the medical kit if one is available.

pre.title: Check response and breathing
pre.detail: If not breathing normally, use the chest pain / collapse protocol.

steps.title: Keep the airway open
steps.detail: Restrain them gently on their side and watch the breathing continuously.

steps.title: Check pupils every 5 minutes
steps.detail: Unequal or unresponsive pupils are a red flag for the ground team.

steps.title: Neuro checks every 15 minutes
steps.detail: Check orientation, speech, pupils, and strength in hands and feet.

steps.title: Watch for red flags
steps.detail: Worsening headache, vomiting, confusion or drowsiness: escalate immediately.

post.title: Priority packet to ground
post.detail: Initial priority alert sent automatically at T+0. Step timeline is transmitted upon completion.

post.title: No critical tasks for 24 h
post.detail: The patient stays off EVAs and critical operations until cleared.

note: Loose objects become projectiles in weightlessness, so secure the area first.

name: Severe allergic reaction
summary: Swelling, hives, or breathing trouble after food, medicine or exposure.

pre.title: Call it out
pre.detail: Announce the emergency. The CMO leads.

pre.title: Remove the trigger
pre.detail: Stop the food or medicine, or move away from the exposure.

steps.title: Epinephrine auto-injector
steps.detail: Use it as written in the onboard anaphylaxis checklist.

steps.title: Oxygen and monitoring
steps.detail: Oxygen per protocol. SpO2 and breathing rate every 5 minutes.

steps.title: Antihistamine per checklist
steps.detail: Follow the onboard allergy checklist.

steps.title: Watch for 4 hours
steps.detail: If breathing or swallowing becomes difficult, switch to the other track.

post.title: Priority packet to ground
post.detail: Initial priority alert sent automatically at T+0. Step timeline is transmitted upon completion.

post.title: Log the trigger
post.detail: Record it so the whole crew can avoid it.

note: Medicines can degrade faster in space radiation. Check expiry dates in the kit.
